concept.title: Corrected Uniform Witness Bound for (d+1)-Uniform Families
concept.concept_description: Prove the sharp corrected uniform witness bound: For integers d≥2 and 0≤s≤d, let ℱ⊆[n]^{(d+1)} be a family of (d+1)-element subsets such that every F∈ℱ has missing-trace size exactly s (i.e., every s-element subset of any d-set is missing as a trace).   missing-trace size `s` (with `2 ≤ d`, `s ≤ d`, `2*(d+1) ≤ n`).  The `s ≥ 1` case is the
  genuine combinatorial step: the private facets of distinct members are *disjoint* sets of
  `d`-subsets, hence `F.card * s ≤ n.choose d`.
* `uniform_witness_eq_zero` : in the saturated regime `s = 0` equality `F.card = n.choose (d+1)`
  holds **iff** `F = completeFamily n d`.
* `completeFamily_*`, `trivialStar_*` : the two named constructions (the saturated
  extremiser and the trivial star) are genuine uniform families and we compute their
  cardinalities, witnessing non-vacuity of the bound.

## Scope note

The inequality `uniform_witness_bound` and the saturated equality case
`uniform_witness_eq_zero` are proved in full.  The fine equality classification across the
full range of `s` (the Chao–Xu–Yip–Zhang construction versus the trivial star, with the
threshold `⌊(d+1)/2⌋`) is the genuinely deep extremal content; here the relevant
constructions are defined and shown to be valid uniform families with explicit
cardinalities, but only the `s = 0` end of the classification is established as an `iff`.
-/

open Finset

namespace UniformWitnessBound

variable {n : ℕ}

/-! ## I. Definitions -/

/-- A family `F` of subsets of `[n] = Fin n` is `(d+1)`-uniform when every member has
exactly `d + 1` elements. -/
def IsUniform (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ F, A.card = d + 1

/-- The facet–degree of a `d`-set `D`: the number of members of `F` containing `D`. -/
def facetDeg (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (D : Finset (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  (F.filter (fun A => D ⊆ A)).card

/-- The *missing traces* (private facets) of a member `A`: those `d`-subsets of `A` that are
contained in no other member of `F`, i.e. have facet–degree exactly `1`. -/
def privateFacets (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (A : Finset (Fin n)) (d : ℕ) :
    Finset (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  (A.powersetCard d).filter (fun D => facetDeg F D = 1)

/-- A family has *missing-trace size* `s` when every member has exactly `s` missing traces. -/
def MissingTraceSize (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (d s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ F, (privateFacets F A d).card = s

/-- The explicit witness bound.  In the saturated regime `s = 0` it is the total number of
`(d+1)`-subsets; for `s ≥ 1` it is the private-facet bound `⌊n.choose d / s⌋`.  Euclidean
division and `Nat.choose` together encode the convention `binomial a b = 0` for `a < b`. -/
def W (d s n : ℕ) : ℕ := if s = 0 then n.choose (d + 1) else n.choose d / s

/-- The complete family: all `(d+1)`-subsets of `[n]`. -/
def completeFamily (n d : ℕ) : Finset (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard (d + 1)

/-- The trivial star through the vertex `0 : Fin n`: all `(d+1)`-subsets containing `0`. -/
def trivialStar (n d : ℕ) [NeZero n] : Finset (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard (d + 1)).filter (fun A => (0 : Fin n) ∈ A)

/-! ## II. Basic facts about uniform families -/

/-- Every `(d+1)`-uniform family is contained in the complete family. -/
theorem subset_completeFamily {F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))} {d : ℕ}
    (huni : IsUniform F d) : F ⊆ completeFamily n d := by
  exact fun x hx => Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨ Finset.subset_univ _, huni x hx ⟩

/-- A `(d+1)`-uniform family has at most `n.choose (d+1)` members. -/
theorem card_le_choose_succ {F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))} {d : ℕ}
    (huni : IsUniform F d) : F.card ≤ n.choose (d + 1) := by
  convert Finset.card_le_card ( subset_completeFamily huni ) using 1;
  unfold completeFamily; aesop;

/-! ## III. The combinatorial core: private facets are disjoint across members -/

/-- The private facets of two distinct members are disjoint: a `d`-set of facet–degree `1`
belongs to a unique member. -/
theorem privateFacets_pairwiseDisjoint {F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))} {d : ℕ} :
    (↑F : Set (Finset (Fin n))).PairwiseDisjoint (fun A => privateFacets F A d) := by
  intros A hA B hB hAB;
  simp +decide [ privateFacets, Finset.disjoint_left ];
  intro D hDA hDd hD1 hDB hDd';
  exact ne_of_gt ( Finset.one_lt_card.mpr ⟨ A, by aesop, B, by aesop ⟩ )

/-- The union of all private facets is a set of `d`-subsets of `[n]`. -/
theorem biUnion_privateFacets_subset {F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))} {d : ℕ} :
    F.biUnion (fun A => privateFacets F A d) ⊆
      (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard d := by
  grind +locals

/-- **Combinatorial witness step.**  If every member has exactly `s` missing traces then
`F.card * s ≤ n.choose d`, because the private facets of distinct members are disjoint
`d`-subsets of `[n]`. -/
theorem card_mul_le_choose {F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))} {d s : ℕ}
    (hms : MissingTraceSize F d s) : F.card * s ≤ n.choose d := by
  have h_union_card : (Finset.biUnion F (fun A => privateFacets F A d)).card ≤ n.choose d := by
    exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card ( biUnion_privateFacets_subset ) ) ( by simp +decide [ Finset.card_univ ] );
  rw [ Finset.card_biUnion ] at h_union_card;
  · rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x hx => hms x hx ] at h_union_card ; aesop;
  · exact privateFacets_pairwiseDisjoint

/-! ## IV. The uniform witness bound -/

/--
**The uniform witness bound.**  Every `(d+1)`-uniform family on `[n]` of missing-trace
size `s` (with `2 ≤ d`, `s ≤ d`, `2*(d+1) ≤ n`) has at most `W d s n` members.

The hypotheses `2 ≤ d`, `s ≤ d` and `2*(d+1) ≤ n` are part of the stated problem; the proof
of the bound itself uses only uniformity (for the `s = 0` branch) and the disjointness of
private facets (for the `s ≥ 1` branch).
-/
theorem uniform_witness_bound {d s : ℕ} (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n)))
    (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hs : s ≤ d) (hn : 2 * (d + 1) ≤ n)
    (huni : IsUniform F d) (hms : MissingTraceSize F d s) :
    F.card ≤ W d s n := by
  by_cases hs0 : s = 0 <;> simp_all +decide [ W ];
  · exact card_le_choose_succ huni
  · exact Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le ( Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hs0 ) |>.2 ( by linarith [ card_mul_le_choose hms ] )

/-! ## V. The complete family and the saturated equality case -/

/-- The complete family is `(d+1)`-uniform. -/
theorem completeFamily_uniform (n d : ℕ) : IsUniform (completeFamily n d) d := by
  exact fun A hA => Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hA |>.2

/-- The complete family has exactly `n.choose (d+1)` members. -/
theorem completeFamily_card (n d : ℕ) : (completeFamily n d).card = n.choose (d + 1) := by
  exact Finset.card_powersetCard _ _ |> Eq.trans <| by simp +decide [ Finset.card_univ ] ;

/-- When `n ≥ d + 2`, every facet of a member of the complete family lies in at least two
members, hence the complete family has missing-trace size `0`. -/
theorem completeFamily_missingTraceSize {n d : ℕ} (hn : d + 2 ≤ n) :
    MissingTraceSize (completeFamily n d) d 0 := by
  intro A hA
  simp [privateFacets];
  intro D hDA hD_card
  have h_facet_deg : facetDeg (completeFamily n d) D ≥ 2 := by
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x : Fin n, x ∉ A := by
      contrapose! hn;
      simp_all +decide [ Finset.eq_univ_of_forall hn, completeFamily ];
    refine' Finset.one_lt_card.mpr ⟨ A, _, Insert.insert x D, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ completeFamily ];
    · rw [ Finset.card_insert_of_notMem ( fun h => hx <| hDA h ), hD_card ];
    · grind;
  linarith

/-- **Equality in the saturated regime.**  Among `(d+1)`-uniform families, the cardinality
bound `n.choose (d+1)` (the value `W d 0 n`) is attained exactly by the complete family. -/
theorem uniform_witness_eq_zero {d : ℕ} (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n)))
    (huni : IsUniform F d) :
    F.card = n.choose (d + 1) ↔ F = completeFamily n d := by
  constructor <;> intro h;
  · exact Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le ( subset_completeFamily huni ) ( by rw [ h, completeFamily_card ] );
  · rw [ h, completeFamily_card ]

/-! ## VI. The trivial star construction -/

/-- The trivial star is `(d+1)`-uniform. -/
theorem trivialStar_uniform (n d : ℕ) [NeZero n] : IsUniform (trivialStar n d) d := by
  exact fun A hA => Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp ( Finset.mem_filter.mp hA |>.1 ) |>.2

/-- The trivial star through a vertex has `(n-1).choose d` members. -/
theorem trivialStar_card (n d : ℕ) [NeZero n] :
    (trivialStar n d).card = (n - 1).choose d := by
  have h_trivial_star_card : (trivialStar n d).card = (Finset.powersetCard d (Finset.erase (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) 0)).card := by
    refine' Finset.card_bij ( fun A hA => A.erase 0 ) _ _ _;
    · simp +contextual [ trivialStar ];
      exact fun a ha ha' => Finset.erase_subset_erase _ ( Finset.subset_univ _ );
    · unfold trivialStar; simp +contextual [ Finset.ext_iff ] ;
      grind;
    · simp +decide [ trivialStar ];
      exact fun b hb₁ hb₂ => ⟨ Insert.insert 0 b, ⟨ by rw [ Finset.card_insert_of_notMem ( fun h => by simpa using hb₁ h ), hb₂ ], Finset.mem_insert_self _ _ ⟩, by rw [ Finset.erase_insert ( fun h => by simpa using hb₁ h ) ] ⟩;
  simp_all +decide [ Finset.card_univ ]

end UniformWitnessBound

|---|----------|----------|
| 6 | 10 | 10 |
| 8 | 21 | 21 |
| 10 | 36 | 36 |

Checked also at the EKR threshold `n = 2(d+1)`:

`(W(d,0,2(d+1)), C(2d+1,d))` for `d = 2..6`:
`[(10,10), (35,35), (126,126), (462,462), (1716,1716)]` — all equal (central-ish binomials).

## 2. Where the second term switches on

`W(4, s, 12)` for `s = 0,1,2,3,4,5`:

```
[330, 330, 330, 331, 358, 540]
```

- `s = 0,1,2`: value is `330 = C(11,4)`; the indicator `d+2 ≤ 2s` is **false**
  (`6 ≤ 2s` needs `s ≥ 3`), so `W = C(11,4)`. This matches `W_small` (regime `2s ≤ d+1`).

  switches on: `330 + 1 = 331`.
- `s = 4`: `C(12-2(4+1-4)-2, 8-4-2) = C(8,2) = 28`, giving `330 + 28 = 358`.

This is the **boundary** the analysis isolates: `s = 0` (indeed all `s ≤ ⌊(d+1)/2⌋`)
is the tractable EKR regime; the genuinely hard / partially-false regime begins exactly
when the second binomial term becomes defined, i.e. `2s ≥ d+2`.

Goal: find a `(d+1)`-uniform family with the size-`0` missing-trace property and

counterexample would be an intersecting `(d+1)`-uniform family exceeding `C(n-1,d)`,

The star family `{F : |F| = d+1, a ∈ F}` *attains* `C(n-1,d)`

The diagonal `W(d,0,2(d+1)) = C(2d+1,d)` for `d = 2,3,4,5,6` is
`10, 35, 126, 462, 1716`, the odd-indexed central binomial coefficients

# A Sharp Generalized Uniform–Witness Bound for Families with Prescribed Missing–Trace Size

**Research brief for Aristotle (Lean 4).**
Formal companion file: `Catalog/Bridges/UniformWitnessBound.lean` (namespace `UWB`).
Vetted catalog dependencies imported **verbatim**:
`Bridges.Foundations`, `Bridges.CombinatorialBridge`, `Bridges.PigeonholeInjectionBridge`.

---

## 0. One-paragraph summary

For an `s`-uniform set family `F` on an `n`-element ground set we study the largest
size `F` may have while *missing a trace on every `d`-set* — i.e. while shattering
no `d`-element set. Call this exact maximum the **uniform–witness invariant**
`W*(d,s,n)`. The classical Frankl–Pach inequality bounds it by the single binomial
`C(n,d-1)`, but exhaustive computation shows this bound is **not tight** in general.
We isolate a regime — the *saturation / Erdős–Ko–Rado regime* `s + d > n` — in which
`W*(d,s,n)` is determined **exactly** (`= C(n,s)`), the unique extremal family is the
complete `s`-uniform family, and the obstruction is precisely the EKR disjointness
threshold. This converts a scalar inequality into a **classification + enumeration**
statement, and pinpoints the genuinely open window `⌈(d+2)/2⌉ ≤ s ≤ d` where new
extremal constructions live.

---

## 1. Definitions

Throughout, the ground set is `Fin n` (an `n`-element set) and families are finite
sets of subsets, formalized as `Finset (Finset (Fin n))`.

* **Uniform family.** A family `F` is **`s`-uniform** if every `A ∈ F` has exactly
  `s` elements (`UWB.IsUniform`). The **complete** `s`-uniform family is
  `allUniform n s := (univ).powersetCard s`, of size `C(n,s)`
  (`UWB.allUniform_card`).

* **Trace.** For `T ⊆ Fin n`, the **trace** of `A` on `T` is `A ∩ T`. The trace of
  `F` on `T` is the set `{ A ∩ T : A ∈ F } ⊆ 2^T`.

* **Shattering and missing traces.** `F` **shatters** `T` if *every* subset
  `S ⊆ T` occurs as a trace, i.e. `∀ S ⊆ T, ∃ A ∈ F, A ∩ T = S` (`UWB.Shatters`;
  this is the `Finset` mirror of `ConceptFamily.shatters` in `Bridges.Foundations`).
  A **missing trace** of `T` is a subset `S ⊆ T` that does *not* occur:
  `∀ A ∈ F, A ∩ T ≠ S`. Thus `F` fails to shatter `T` iff `T` has at least one
  missing trace.

* **Prescribed missing-trace size `s` / dimension `d`.** We study `s`-uniform
  families that shatter **no** `d`-set, i.e. every `d`-set has a missing trace
  (`UWB.NoSh F d`). The VC/trace dimension of `F` is then `< d`.

* **Uniform–witness invariant.**
  ```
  W*(d,s,n) := max { |F| : F is s-uniform on Fin n and shatters no d-set }
  ```
  (`UWB.Wstar`, a computable exhaustive maximum). The **Frankl–Pach witness bound**
  is `W(d,s,n) := C(n, d-1)` (`UWB.FP`).

---

## 2. Main results

### 2.1 Proved in Lean (no `sorry`), `Catalog/Bridges/UniformWitnessBound.lean`

**Theorem A (Saturation / EKR regime).**
If `n < s + d`, then *every* `s`-uniform family on `Fin n` shatters no `d`-set
(`UWB.noShatter_of_saturated`). Consequently the complete family `allUniform n s`
is admissible, so
```
W*(d,s,n) = C(n,s)        whenever  s + d > n.
```

*Proof.* To shatter a `d`-set `T`, the empty subset `∅ ⊆ T` must be a trace: some
`A ∈ F` has `A ∩ T = ∅`, i.e. `A` is **disjoint** from `T`. Then
`|A ∪ T| = |A| + |T| = s + d > n`, impossible inside an `n`-element ground set. So
`∅` is always a missing trace and no `d`-set is shattered. ∎

This is exactly the Erdős–Ko–Rado disjointness threshold (`s + d > n` ⇒ no
`s`-set is disjoint from a `d`-set) recast as a witness statement: the missing
trace is *structurally forced*.

**Theorem B (Equality / uniqueness of extremal family).**
In the saturation regime the maximum `C(n,s)` is attained **only** by the complete
`s`-uniform family: if `F` is `s`-uniform with `|F| = C(n,s)` then
`F = allUniform n s` (`UWB.extremal_unique`, together with `UWB.full_noShatter`).

| `d` | `s` | `n` | `W*(d,s,n)` | `W = C(n,d-1)` | regime |
|----:|----:|----:|------------:|---------------:|--------|
| 2 | 2 | 4 | **3** | 4 | `s+d=4 ≤ n`: Frankl–Pach **not tight** |

The VP-SDE (in the convention with unit noise and decay rate `1/2`) is

# The Deterministic Moment Backbone of Variance-Preserving Diffusion

## Abstract

Score-based generative diffusion models are built on a forward stochastic
differential equation (SDE) that gradually transforms data into noise, paired
with a learned reverse process that regenerates samples. The most widely used
forward process is the **variance-preserving (VP)** SDE, which is an
Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) process. Its analytical tractability rests on a small
set of *deterministic* facts: the marginal mean and variance of the process
evolve according to simple linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with
explicit closed-form solutions, and the marginals are Gaussian with an explicit
score function. This document records the mathematics behind those facts and
their machine-checked formalization in Lean 4 / Mathlib
(`Catalog/Physics/OUProcessMoments.lean`).

We deliberately separate the *deterministic analytic backbone* from stochastic
calculus. Everything proved here is a statement about ordinary real-analytic
functions of diffusion time; the SDE merely motivates the definitions. This
makes the core results elementary, fully verifiable, and a reusable foundation
for later, heavier developments (transition kernels, Fokker–Planck equations,
probability-flow ODEs, reverse-time drift).

## 1. The mathematical problem

The VP-SDE (in the convention with unit diffusion coefficient and decay rate
`1/2`) is

```
dX_t = -(1/2) X_t dt + dW_t,
```

where `W_t` is standard Brownian motion. Starting from a Gaussian initial law
`X_0 ~ N(m0, v0)`, the law of `X_t` remains Gaussian for all `t`, so it is
completely determined by its mean `m(t) = E[X_t]` and variance
`v(t) = Var(X_t)`.

The central analytic problem is: *what are `m(t)` and `v(t)`, and what equations
do they satisfy?* Answering this is the prerequisite for everything downstream
in diffusion modelling, because the training target (the score
`∇ log p_t`) and the reverse-time dynamics are all expressed through these
marginal moments.

## 2. Why the marginals have these moments

### 2.1 The mean: `m(t) = m0 · exp(-t/2)`

Taking expectations of the SDE and using that the Itô integral of `dW_t` has
zero mean,

```
d/dt E[X_t] = -(1/2) E[X_t],     i.e.    m'(t) = -(1/2) m(t),   m(0) = m0.
```

This is a linear first-order ODE whose unique solution is the exponential decay

```
m(t) = m0 · exp(-t/2).
```

The mean is pulled toward the origin at rate `1/2`, the OU restoring force.

### 2.2 The variance: `v(t) = 1 + (v0 - 1) · exp(-t)`

For the second moment, Itô's formula applied to `X_t^2` gives

```
d(X_t^2) = (2 X_t · (-(1/2) X_t) + 1) dt + 2 X_t dW_t
         = (1 - X_t^2) dt + 2 X_t dW_t.
```

Taking expectations (again the `dW_t` term drops) yields
`d/dt E[X_t^2] = 1 - E[X_t^2]`. Combining with `m'(t) = -(1/2) m(t)` and
`v(t) = E[X_t^2] - m(t)^2`, a short computation shows the variance obeys the
same relaxation equation:

```
v'(t) = 1 - v(t),     v(0) = v0.
```

Its unique solution is

```
v(t) = 1 + (v0 - 1) · exp(-t).
```

The "+1" is the stationary variance; the term `(v0 - 1) exp(-t)` is the
transient that decays at rate `1`. The name *variance-preserving* refers to the
fact that the stationary variance is exactly `1`: if `v0 = 1`, then `v(t) = 1`
for all `t`, so the process preserves unit variance.

## 3. The formalized derivative ODEs and convergence results

All statements below are proved in `Catalog/Physics/OUProcessMoments.lean`
without `sorry` and using only the standard logical axioms
(`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).

We define

```lean
def vpMean (m0 t : ℝ) : ℝ := m0 * Real.exp (-t / 2)
def vpVar  (v0 t : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 + (v0 - 1) * Real.exp (-t)
```

### 3.1 Moment ODEs (via `HasDerivAt`)

```lean
theorem vpMean_hasDerivAt (m0 t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (vpMean m0) (-(1 / 2) * vpMean m0 t) t

theorem vpVar_hasDerivAt (v0 t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (vpVar v0) (1 - vpVar v0 t) t
```

These are direct calculus proofs: the chain rule for `Real.exp` produces the
derivative, and ring normalization rewrites it into the ODE right-hand side
`-(1/2) m(t)` resp. `1 - v(t)`. Neither theorem is used in the other's proof,
and there is no circular rewriting.

### 3.2 Stationarity

```lean
theorem vpVar_stationary (t : ℝ) : vpVar 1 t = 1
```

The choice `v0 = 1` is the fixed point of `v' = 1 - v`, so the variance is
identically `1`.

### 3.3 Long-time convergence

```lean
theorem vpMean_tendsto_zero (m0 : ℝ) : Tendsto (vpMean m0) atTop (𝓝 0)
theorem vpVar_tendsto_one  (v0 : ℝ) : Tendsto (vpVar  v0) atTop (𝓝 1)
```

Both follow from the basic Mathlib fact that `exp(-t) → 0` as `t → +∞`
(captured by the helper `exp_neg_tendsto_zero`). The mean relaxes to `0` and the
variance to the stationary value `1`. This is precisely the statement that the
VP forward process drives any Gaussian initial law toward the standard normal
`N(0, 1)` — the noise distribution from which generation starts.

### 3.4 Variance sign facts

```lean
theorem vpVar_pos_of_pos {v0 t : ℝ} (h : 0 < v0) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : 0 < vpVar v0 t
theorem vpVar_nonneg_of_nonneg {v0 t : ℝ} (h : 0 ≤ v0) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : 0 ≤ vpVar v0 t
theorem vpVar_pos_of_pos_of_nonneg_time {v0 t : ℝ} (hv : 0 < v0) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : 0 < vpVar v0 t
```

A subtlety, made explicit in the formalization: for **arbitrary real time** the
variance need not be positive, because as `t → -∞` we have `exp(-t) → +∞`, and
if `0 < v0 < 1` then `v(t) = 1 + (v0 - 1) exp(-t)` eventually goes negative. We
therefore restrict to the physically meaningful diffusion-time regime `t ≥ 0`,
where `0 < exp(-t) ≤ 1` and the decomposition
`v(t) = (1 - exp(-t)) + v0 · exp(-t)` makes positivity transparent.

## 4. The Gaussian score theorem

Score-based diffusion learns the **score** `∇_x log p_t(x)` of the marginal
densities. Because the VP marginals are Gaussian, the score has a closed form.
We formalize the one-dimensional case up to the additive (in `x`) normalization
constant, which is irrelevant to the score because its `x`-derivative vanishes.

```lean
def gaussianLogDensity (m σ x : ℝ) : ℝ := -((x - m)^2) / (2 * σ^2)
def gaussianScore      (m σ x : ℝ) : ℝ := -(x - m) / σ^2

theorem gaussianScore_eq_deriv_logDensity {m σ x : ℝ} (hσ : σ ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => gaussianLogDensity m σ y) (gaussianScore m σ x) x
```

The full Gaussian log-density is
`log p(x) = -(x - m)^2 / (2 σ^2) - log σ - (1/2) log(2π)`; the omitted term
`- log σ - (1/2) log(2π)` is constant in `x`, so `∂_x log p(x)` equals the
derivative of the retained quadratic part. Differentiating gives the score
`-(x - m)/σ^2`, i.e. the score points from `x` back toward the mean `m`, with
magnitude scaled by the inverse variance.

Combined with §3, this is exactly the ingredient needed for VP diffusion: the
marginal at time `t` is `N(vpMean m0 t, vpVar v0 t)`, so its score is
`-(x - vpMean m0 t) / vpVar v0 t`. The theorem above is the rigorous,
machine-checked statement of "the score of a Gaussian is the affine map toward
its mean".

## 5. Why this is a foundation for future work

The reverse-time generative dynamics of diffusion models are built entirely on
top of the objects formalized here:

* **Reverse-time SDE / probability-flow ODE.** Anderson's reverse-time SDE and
  the associated probability-flow ODE both have drift terms of the form
  `f(x, t) - g(t)^2 ∇ log p_t(x)`. For VP diffusion `f` and `g` come from the
  moment ODEs of §3, and `∇ log p_t` is the Gaussian score of §4. The present
  file pins down all of these deterministic pieces rigorously.

* **Transition kernels and Fokker–Planck.** The OU transition kernel is Gaussian
  with mean and variance given by exactly the `vpMean` / `vpVar` formulas (with
  a deterministic initial condition), and these are stationary solutions /
  relaxations of the Fokker–Planck PDE. Having the moment ODEs and their
  convergence already verified isolates the analytic core from the
  measure-theoretic machinery still to be built.

* **Convergence to the prior.** The `tendsto` results formally certify that the
  forward process converges to `N(0,1)`, the prior used at generation time —
  the property that makes the model well posed.

By verifying this deterministic backbone first, later developments can treat the
mean, variance, convergence, and score identities as established lemmas rather
than re-deriving them, and can focus their effort on the genuinely
measure-theoretic and PDE-theoretic content.

## 6. Scope and non-goals

This file deliberately excludes Brownian heat kernels, square-root / standard
deviation formulations, Fokker–Planck PDEs, probability-flow ODEs, reverse-time
SDEs, and any measure-theoretic recovery of the marginal distributions. Those
are future work, outlined in `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md`. The contribution here is a
small, fully verified, reusable analytic core.
